text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.2% today to $136.09, recovering modestly after a steep 8% slide over the past two weeks. The rebound came as Brent crude oil dipped below $90 a barrel for the first time since August—a move driven by Trump's statements suggesting the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon," which eased concerns about broader Middle East supply disruptions. Even so, the stock remains well below its $144 level from early November, when the company reported quarterly results.

The narrower picture shows tension between two forces: oil prices falling (bad for a producer's near-term revenue) but geopolitical risk receding (which can reduce long-term uncertainty). US crude trades at $99.64 while Brent sits at $107, so the global-to-domestic spread is still wide—suggesting markets see more supply pressure overseas than domestically. The company's slide from early November likely reflects both the softer energy prices and market digestion of the quarterly report filed that week.
